newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 72,000t corn/12,000t soybeans. [CORRECTED 05:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 72,000t corn/12,000t soybeans. [CORRECTED 05:54 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects the size of the tender for corn from 76,000t in the headline and the text.)
Taiwan will hold a tender for at least 72,000 tonnes of corn and 12,000 tonnes of soybeans from the United States, grain traders said on Friday.
The state-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp is expected to tender late next week for a combined shipment of 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans, the traders said.
Delivery from the U.S. Gulf of Mexico is from October 25 to November 10.
Taiwan's FGEP group is also in the market for a 54,000 tonne corn shipment to be delivered in December, traders said.
The FGEP group is made up of Fwu Sow Grain, Great Wall Enterprise, President Enterprise and Ever Smile Feed Mill Co.
Local buyers said pressures from the imminent U.S. corn harvest season and the lack of strong weather concerns could keep the corn prices low.

"Corn will remain bearish for nearby harvest season as long as no serious frost comes into play," an executive at Taiwan's Formosa Oilseed said. Formosa Oilseed is a key buyer in Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group.
Local Pacific Northwest freight cost was about US$10.00 per tonne and the Gulf of Mexico cost is about US$20.55 per tonne, both for Panamax-sized November and December shipments, dealers said.
